name: Ta Gou Ta Doi 搭九搭对
description: Ta Gou Ta Doi (搭九搭对, 'making nines and pairs') is a Malaysian rummy-like game played with 32 Chinese chess (Xiangqi) pieces used as cards. Each turn: draw one, discard one. Win by collecting three valid sets of two: Gou (two pieces summing to 9) or Doi (pair of same value). Easy and hard variants differ in what counts as a set.

content.text: Ta Gou Ta Doi (搭九搭对, 'making nines and pairs') is a Malaysian rummy-like game played with 32 Chinese chess (Xiangqi) pieces used as cards. Each turn: draw one, discard one. Win by collecting three valid sets of two: Gou (two pieces summing to 9) or Doi (pair of same value). Easy and hard variants differ in what counts as a set.
Malaysian game using Xiangqi pieces as playing cards. Name (Fuzhou dialect) means 'making nines and pairs'. Documentation from Alexey Lobashev and Hua Kiong's blog.
32 Xiangqi pieces mixed face down, arranged in stacks of two in a circle.
Chinese chess (Xiangqi) set of 32 pieces; table.

Starting player determined by turning one stack face up and counting by total value. Players take stacks clockwise until each has two stacks; first player takes a third stack, then each takes one piece from next stacks so each has 5 pieces. Pieces held face down in a row.

items.text: Easy: Gou: two pieces of any rank and colour whose values add up to 9. Doi: two pieces of the same value, any colour.
Hard: Only valid sets are pairs of identical pieces (same colour) or the value-2 pair (marshal and general).
